401858540.summary: Every source read picks Ohio State (7-4) to win at home, but most expect a close, low-scoring game. The line has dropped from 13.5 to about 10-10.5, the total is 37.5-38.5 and the moneyline is about OSU -395 to -430. The case for Ohio State is Jeremiah Smith, the nation's receiving leader, against a Michigan offense ranked 112th in EPA per play and 129th in scoring (18.3 points per game). Ohio State starts freshman Luke Fahey with Julian Sayin out, has lost three of four (including at Nebraska) and is 0-4 against the spread in its last four. The split is on the spread: SI Betting lays the 10, while CBS (six of nine CBS experts on Michigan ATS) and Predictem take Michigan +10.5. Michigan QB Bryce Underwood (hamstring) is questionable but expected to start.

401862842.summary: Every source that names a winner picks Navy (4-6), which has won two straight, most recently 38-34 over Memphis with 335 rushing yards. Charlotte (1-10) has lost four in a row, the last 42-14 at Tulsa, and is 0-5 at home. The key matchup is Navy's run game (302.3 rush yards and 30.1 points per game) against a Charlotte defense allowing 184.7 rush yards and 36.7 points per game. The worries for Navy are a defense allowing 30.8 points per game, an 0-4 road record and a possible letdown before Army. Spread picks split: PickDawgz takes Navy -16.5, while Doc's Sports takes Charlotte +14.5 and BetMGM's model leans Charlotte to cover. Moneylines run about -750 to -900 and models give Navy roughly 83-89%. No injuries were reported for either team.

401856758.summary: Every source expects LSU (6-5, 3-5 SEC) to win at Arkansas (4-7, 2-6 SEC), but they split on the 14.5-point spread. Tiger Rag's three staff picks have LSU winning by 21-28 and Pick Dawgz lays the points; Yahoo (23-20) and Beatline (24-17) predict a closer LSU win, and Doc's Sports takes Arkansas +12.5. LSU has lost three straight, all as favorites, but each of its six wins came by 21 or more. Arkansas has lost five in a row, most recently 45-3 at Texas; it scores 19.7 points per game (124th) and allows 4.4 yards per carry, worst in the SEC, against an LSU defense allowing 266.5 yards per game. LSU WRs Jackson Harris and Winston Watkins Jr. are questionable again. Yahoo adds that neither team has much to play for, which could keep it close.

401871063.summary: Every source picks No. 21 Liberty (10-1, 7-0 CUSA, ten straight wins) to win outright, with projected scores from 31-14 to 38-24. Liberty's case is its run game (221 rushing yards per game, 9th in FBS; Kam Davis has 821 yards) against a Missouri State defense allowing 180.1 rushing yards and 28.7 points per game, plus a Liberty defense allowing 14.5, best in CUSA. The split is on the margin: Missouri State is 4-1 at home, has covered four straight and nearly beat Jacksonville State, so Doc's Sports takes the Bears +14.5 and Predictem advises against laying 17.5. Totals picks split (Predictem Under 53.5, Cappers Picks Over 52.5). No Liberty injuries were named; one AI aggregator lists three Missouri State players out for the season.

401856765.summary: Four of five previews back Tennessee to win and cover -13.5. Their case rests on a defense allowing 14.2 points per game that held LSU to 13 last week, and a run game averaging 213 yards against a Vanderbilt run defense ranked 92nd in opponent EPA per rush. Tennessee is 9-2, playing for a playoff spot and on three straight wins; Vanderbilt is 4-7 (1-7 SEC) after a 34-27 loss at Florida, its fourth loss in five. RB DeSean Bishop (lower body) and LB Arion Carter are questionable on Tennessee's Nov 26 report, and Vanderbilt QB Jared Curtis was hurt late at Florida but is expected to play. The contrarian is Rocky Top Insider's model: Tennessee by 12 (80.8%), so it takes Vanderbilt +13.5.

401858312.summary: No track: Duke is ESPN FPI #25 (power gate). All seven previews pick Wake Forest (10-1, already in the ACC title game) to win, with predicted scores from 27-14 to 38-21. They point to an offense leading the nation at 44.5 points per game, Gio Lopez (21 TD, 1 INT) and seven straight wins by 21+. Duke (7-4) has lost two straight and gained only 247 yards in a 20-10 loss to Clemson, when Walker Eget went 16 of 38 for 149 yards. Wake RB Ty Clark III is out for the season. Against the spread the sources split: Predictem and Pick Dawgz lay -14.5, while WagerTalk, Knup and Doc's back Duke +14.5, citing Duke's top-10 scoring defense (15.7 allowed), its four straight series wins and Wake having little reason to run up the score.
